newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key TIFFE Euroyen futures flat despite JGBs' rise.
newsitem.headline: Key TIFFE Euroyen futures flat despite JGBs' rise.

text.p: The key June three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures on TIFFE ended Thursday's day session unchanged, despite Japanese government bond futures' bull-run.
The key December JGB futures contract closed up 0.29 at 125.48, a record high for any benchmark JGB futures contract.
"Unlike JGB futures, the upside limit for Euroyen futures is quite clear. One can't expect Euroyen futures' yield curve to flatten at the same pace as JGBs'," a city bank trader said.
Turnover was 24,751 contracts for the benchmark June contract and 23,317 for the September.
In the morning session, the September's turnover exceeded that of June.
The September contract closed at 99.15, down from 99.16 on Wednesday.
"Unless JGB futures fall sharply, it is difficult to take short positions. Hence, Euroyen futures are likely to remain stuck in a very narrow range for a while," said the trader.
There was talk that foreign players were selling Euroyen futures and buying JGB futures today, traders said.
In the interbank call market, the key unsecured overnight rate eased slightly in the afternoon, after trading at 0.50 percent in the morning.
Wednesday's weighted average of the overnight rate was 0.49 percent.
This morning's uptick in the overnight rate was largely due to month-end fund demand, traders said.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) injected a net 200 billion yen into the money market in its regular morning operation, maintaining a neutral stance.
About 60 billion yen worth of the key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.51 percent.
On Wednesday, three-month CDs were issued at 0.51 and 0.52 percent.
About 45 billion yen worth of one-month CDs were issued at 0.49 percent, unchanged from Wednesday.
Two-month CDs were offered at 0.50 percent, also unchanged from the previous day.
